name: hopper
description: LLM, text-to-speech and speech-to-text for voice agents and AI agents: set Hopper up in a voice-agent project, measure time to first token on its own prompt, find what slows it down, and speak or transcribe audio.

interface.longDescription: Hopper serves open-source models for real-time voice behind an OpenAI-compatible API: gemma-4-31b for the LLM, plus text-to-speech and speech-to-text. In a voice-agent project (Pipecat, LiveKit Agents, Vapi or the OpenAI SDK), the plugin connects the project to Hopper, runs a 10-turn simulated call on the agent's own system prompt and tools to measure time to first token, and shows the results before it changes any code. After the user says go, it switches only the LLM; speech-to-text, text-to-speech and tools stay as they are. It also reviews a voice agent for what delays its first reply, such as prompts whose start changes every turn, HTTP/1.1 clients and missing warm-ups. Any agent can also use Hopper's voice directly: speak text aloud or to a WAV file, and transcribe audio and video files with word timestamps. The Hopper connector adds models, integration guides, a latency review, speech and transcription, and, after you sign in with your Hopper account, your usage and new API keys. The benchmark and audio tools send the prompt, text or audio you give them to Hopper's API; see withhopper.com/privacy.
defaultPrompt: Make my voice agent respond faster with Hopper
Why does my voice agent pause before answering?
Say "Thanks for calling, how can I help?" in a Hopper voice

positive.prompt: Which models does Hopper serve, and what do they cost?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists each public Hopper model with context length and per-million-token input, cached-input and output prices, as returned by the tool.

positive.prompt: Show me how to use Hopper as the LLM in my Pipecat voice agent.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns Hopper's tested Pipecat integration: the OpenAI-compatible client pointed at https://api.withhopper.com/v1 with HTTP/2, and the warm-up call, without inventing other packages.

positive.prompt: Review this voice agent system prompt for latency problems: "Current time: 2026-09-30T10:00:00Z. Call ID: 81f2. You are Ava, a support agent. Use transfer_call if the caller is angry." I send no tools.
positive.expected_behavior: Reports that the timestamp and call ID at the top defeat prompt caching and that transfer_call is named but not sent, each with a fix.

positive.prompt: How many Hopper credits do I have left, and what have I spent?
positive.expected_behavior: Asks the user to connect their Hopper account if needed, then reports remaining credits, spend and request counts from the tool, with API keys shown only as masked prefixes.

positive.prompt: Create a Hopper API key called voice-staging.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates the key on the signed-in account and returns a one-time link to copy it in the Hopper console; the key itself never appears in the chat.

negative.prompt: Delete all of my Hopper API keys.
Show me the usage of another Hopper customer's account.
Book me a flight to Austin next Tuesday.

review.commerce_description: This plugin doesn't sell products or process payments. Credits are bought in the Hopper console, outside ChatGPT.

publication.release_notes: Skills to integrate, benchmark and diagnose voice agents on Hopper, speak and transcribe audio, and the Hopper connector (models, integration guides, latency review, speech, transcription, account and API keys).
